Subject: Post-demo: Acme integration & rate limits

Hi Alex / Priya 

Thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can align on the integration plan: 

Summary of the call:
- Goal: add Redwood-powered semantic search and chat for Acme's product docs + support knowledge base.
- Primary concerns: auth, per-tenant routing, and rate limiting (SLA + retry semantics).
- Workload: ~300 qps during peak support spikes, with many short embedding calls for reranking and occasional longer chat sessions.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) Engineering sync: Ben/Rishi + your infra folks to walk SDK auth and routing patterns.
2) Rate limits doc: we'll share our recommended quotas, 429 handling, and idempotency guidance (see attachments).
3) Pilot: 2-week sandbox with dedicated capacity for Acme to validate latency and costs.

Ben / Rishi — I flagged the items we need from your side (below). Alex / Priya — let me know available windows for an engineering call next week.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0147

Thanks Marissa 

This is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- For routing, we want per-tenant model overrides (certain customers opt into higher-quality variants). Can Redwood support tenant-level routing or do we need separate API keys?
- On auth: we prefer to use our KMS for key material and integrate with short-lived tokens rather than long-lived API keys. Is that supported in the Private deployment?
- Rate limits: can you outline recommended retry/backoff behavior for 429 vs 503? We prefer client-side backoff first, then server-side queuing if needed.

Available windows for an engineering sync: Mon 7/13 10am-12pm PT or Tue 7/14 2pm-4pm PT.

Appreciate it,
Alex
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme Inc

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@acme.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Acme integration & rate limits

Alex 

Quick engineering notes ahead of the sync:

1) Auth & tokens:
- Private deployment supports customer KMS/HSM for key wrapping; we can issue short-lived session tokens that exchange against your KMS-backed identity provider. For hosted mode, we use API keys with RBAC; we can also support OAuth bearer tokens via SSO integrations.

2) Routing / tenant overrides:
- We recommend per-tenant routing via our routing table (tenant_id header) rather than multiple API keys. This lets you pin model variants per tenant and configure fallbacks for capacity constraints. We'll show examples in the SDK.

3) SDK setup / structured output / tool-calling:
- Our SDKs (Python/Node) support tool-calling via structured JSON output and will validate against your schema. We'll include a sample prompt shim for generating a tool-call envelope and a retry-safe request_id header.

4) Embeddings & rerankers:
- For semantic search we recommend storing embeddings with vector-dimension X (will confirm). Reranking should be done client-side by fetching top-N candidates from DB and calling the Redwood reranker endpoint with a stable request_id to enable idempotent scoring if retries occur.

5) Rate limiting, retries & idempotency (short):
- 429 responses: client should implement exponential backoff with jitter. Use the request_id header we return to de-duplicate retries.
- For non-idempotent write operations, use our idempotency-key header so the server can safely ignore duplicates.
- We'll share sample backoff code and recommended thresholds (see attached rate-limit-sla.xlsx).

I'll bring a short slide deck to the engineer sync that includes SDK snippets and header examples.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: trace-429.log (sample of a 429 spike pattern)

From: Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@acme.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Jones <alex.jones@acme.io>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Acme integration & rate limits

Thanks Ben 

Helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our infra/security team:

- Can you confirm the headers/fields returned on 429 that help with client backoff (Retry-After, x-redwood-rate-limit-reset)?
- For idempotency, does the idempotency-key scope to tenant or account? We need to ensure cross-tenant collisions are impossible.
- For embeddings throughput: what's the recommended batch size to maximize GPU utilization without hurting tail latency?

Also, can you pre-share the SDK sample that shows how to attach request_id and idempotency-key in retries? If possible, we'd like to hand that to our backend team before the sync.

Best,
Priya
Staff SRE | Acme Inc

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@acme.io>, Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@acme.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Acme integration & rate limits

Perfect 

Thanks everyone. Quick confirmations and next steps: 

- 429 payloads: we return Retry-After (seconds) when applicable and x-redwood-rate-limit-reset (unix epoch ms). We'll include both in the SDK helper so clients can pick the most reliable signal.
- Idempotency-key: scoped to account_id + idempotency_key namespace; cross-tenant collisions are prevented by including tenant/account in the server-side keyspace.
- Embeddings batch guidance: start with 64-128 vectors per batch for ACME's expected sizes; Ben/Rishi will validate with a short perf run in the sandbox.

Action items:
- Ben/Rishi: send SDK snippet + backoff sample and a short perf note by EOD Tue (7/14).
- Marissa: set up engineer sync Mon 7/13 10am PT (confirmed) and share calendar invite + sandbox access (will send link).
- Alex/Priya: share any compliance constraints for the sandbox (data retention, PII masking).

I've attached the integration guide and SLA spreadsheet. Ben will add the SDK examples to the shared Drive link.

Calendar invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=acme-redwood-engineer-sync
Drive: https://acme.gdrive/shared/Redwood-Integration-Notes

Talk soon
